Subject: Mutual plan & commercial milestones for Redwood POC

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The team is keen to validate performance and cost before we commit to a broader rollout. To keep our procurement and architecture tracks aligned, can we put a short mutual success plan together that ties evaluation milestones to the commercial commitments (pricing tiers, ramp, and renewal uplift)?

High level we want:
- 2-week functional POC (accuracy & integration checks)
- 4-week scale test (latency & throughput at target QPS)
- Production ramp plan (week-by-week traffic gates)

Procurement will need a clear path to approve a committed spend and an expected discount schedule at initial purchase and at renewal if we expand. We aim to finalize the commercial side by the end of Q1 (target close: 2026-03-31).

Can you propose a MAP with milestone-linked pricing and a renewal uplift mechanism? Also please include required deliverables for our security/compliance team (SOC2 evidence, audit logs).

Olivia
Head of AI Platforms
Nebula Analytics

Subject: Re: Mutual plan & commercial milestones for Redwood POC

Olivia —

Really appreciate the clarity. I attached a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) plus a draft term sheet and SOW to get us started. Quick summary below so you can share with procurement:

MAP summary (proposed)
- Week 0-2: Integration & functional POC. Redwood provides model endpoints (hosted), example prompts, and a test harness. Success: agreed accuracy/QA checklist signed off by Nebula engineering.
- Week 3-6: Scale test at target QPS (continuous batching on). Success: 95th percentile latency < 220ms and token cost within agreed target.
- Week 7-12: Production ramp to 100% of initial committed throughput. Weekly ramp gates tied to performance metrics and billing start for committed capacity at gate 3.

Commercial (term-sheet highlights)
- Initial commitment: 12-month term, committed monthly throughput equivalent to 500M tokens/month at an introductory discount of 22% off list for committed spend.
- Ramp: billing for committed capacity begins when the production ramp reaches 60% of committed throughput (Gate 3). Prior to that, usage billed at on-demand list rates.
- Renewal uplift: if Nebula expands committed spend by >=25% year-over-year at renewal, we commit to an incremental discount on the uplifted portion: +3% for 25-49% growth, +6% for 50-99% growth, and +10% for >=100% growth. These uplift discounts apply only to the additional committed spend, not the base.
- Performance protection: if 95th percentile latency exceeds SLA for two consecutive weeks, Redwood will provide a service credit and a free optimization sprint.

Security/compliance: attaching SOC2 summary, audit log export template, and standard DPA language in the SOW.

Next steps:
1) Let us know which MAP milestones you want firm acceptance criteria on (I included checklist items in the attached PDF).
2) We'll incorporate procurement feedback and return a DocuSign-ready term sheet.

Attachments: 2026-02-11_Redwood_MAP_draft.pdf; SOW-Nebula-v1.docx; term-sheet-nebula-20260211.pdf

—

Evan/Olivia —

Appreciate the specificity — we've tightened the term-sheet language and added a worked example in the attached term-sheet PDF. Summary of the clarifications below:

Renewal uplift clarification (explicit)
- The uplift discount applies only to the incremental committed spend above the then-current base committed quantity. No retroactive discounts on prior committed spend. We'll add a definition: "incremental committed spend" = (renewal_committed_quantity - prior_committed_quantity) * list_price.

Example calculation (worked):
- Prior committed throughput: 6M tokens/month; Renewal committed throughput proposed: 8M tokens/month (33% growth).
- Incremental portion = 2M tokens/month. On the incremental portion we apply +3% uplift discount (33% growth falls in 25-49% band).
- If list price = $0.0002/token, incremental monthly list value = 2,000,000 * $0.0002 = $400. Incremental discount = 3% * $400 = $12/month saving on the uplifted portion; new effective price on increment = $0.000194/token.

Commercial guardrails we added per internal request:
- Maximum aggregate uplift discount exposure capped at 15% of ARR for the account unless exec approval is granted.
- Any uplift >50% requires a commercial review and a capacity-planning sign-off to ensure we can reserve GPU pools.

Timeline and next steps:
- We can produce a DocuSign-ready term sheet within 48 hours of your confirmation of functional acceptance criteria.
- Once term sheet is signed, we target POC kickoff within 3 business days and follow the MAP milestones.

Attachments: updated term-sheet-nebula-20260219.pdf (includes worked example), updated MAP pdf (minor edits).

If this matches your expectations, please confirm and I'll send the DocuSign link.

Thanks — talk soon.
